ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: the colony's animals
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: What the colony's people want for their animals, the stories and choices that come of them, and the herd's year.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Give the old dog the warm spot by the fire. Someone will notice.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
The colony's animals are part of its life in Rimfolk, not only its larder and its guard. Someone milking or taming talks to the animal in front of them, a bonded dog falls in at its person's heels, a birth in the herd is news, and an old companion's death is grieved and remembered. Colonists who love animals ask for things that help the herd and their own animals; the council faces hard choices about them in hungry weeks and bad nights; and the herdmaster looks after the people who look after them.
The everyday parts follow the setting "Pets as companions" (People). With PokéWorld, Pokémon count as the colony's animals everywhere on this page, and have a page of their own besides.

table.li: What | When

A word to an animal | Someone milking, shearing, taming, training, tending, feeding or roping an animal in view says something to it, and a child at leisure talks to the animal beside them. These share the once-a-day rate of everything said on screen.
At its person's heels | A bonded animal with nothing to do, near its person, follows them about for a while (not one roped, penned or at work).
A birth in the herd | News, with the mother's name. The colony's first is a day on the calendar.
A death | A named animal's death gets a farewell from the one who loved it, with lines of their own for an old animal that died at the end of a long life and for a Pokémon.

Talk between colonists | Two people who keep animals talk shop (some practice for both), two with bonded animals swap stories, and a child asks a keeper about the animals. Face to face, as all such moments are.
Social events | A keeper shows a child the animals (the two grow closer, and the child learns something), and someone lends a herder a hand with the herd (friendship, and practice).

Small habits | Someone who loves animals and has a herd to watch, or a child, sits out with the herd for a while by day; someone who loves animals or is bonded to a big one brushes down a horse or another big animal of theirs, a little handling practice. Both need "Small habits" on.

li.heading: The herdmaster
li.text: With "Systems talk to each other" on, the herdmaster goes down to the pens within the day to give each newborn a name, if it has none. When someone's animal is sick or hurt, the herdmaster finds them in their free time and tells them how it's doing, face to face: their strain eases a little and the two grow a little closer. About once a week, someone keen on animals who is four levels or more behind the herdmaster is taken along for the day's work, a lesson on the map. Besides, as before, the herdmaster sits with anyone whose named animal dies and minds the animals of those away.

li.heading: Wishes

table.li: Wish | Who asks | Granted

An animal of my own | A grown colonist who loves animals (a passion, a kind soul, a lonely one) and has none, when one of the colony's grown animals has no master. Promised, they're made its master. | +3 mood for 6 days

A barn for the herd | Someone who loves animals, the herdmaster or a kind soul, when the colony's herd of 3 or more sleeps out (likelier in the cold seasons). Fulfilled when one barn has animal beds or sleeping spots for most of the herd, from 2 to 6. | Some contentment and a journal line, no mood

Something to ride | Only with Giddy-Up 2: a hunter, a restless soul or someone who loves animals, with no mount of their own. A rideable animal of the colony's with no master is made theirs when promised; otherwise one is tamed for them. | +3 for 5 days

A favourite kind of animal | Someone fond of animals (a passion, an animal lover, a child, a kind or lonely soul) has always loved one kind: one of those this land has, or that is roaming the map, that the colony's best handler has the skill to tame. The same person keeps the same favourite while the land's animals stay the same. Promised, a calm one out there is marked for taming. With PokéWorld, a favourite Pokémon the same way, caught in a ball. | Fulfilled when the colony has one: joy, a feeling and a journal line, no mood. If it bonds to them later (while the council's promise is watched), a second moment: "it chose me"

A pack animal of my own | A hauler (hauling first in their work), someone with a passion for talk and trade, or a restless soul, with no pack animal of their own, where the colony has one with no master or the land has pack animals it could tame. Promised, the colony's spare one answers to them, else a calm wild one is marked for taming. | Some handling practice and contentment, no mood

li.after: Nobody whose ideoligion abhors bonding with animals asks for these, and nobody whose ideoligion frowns on ranching asks for a barn.

table.li: Goal | For | Done when
A champion at my side | Someone who can fight, with an animal of their own or a love of animals | An animal of theirs has fought beside them in 3 of the colony's battles
A great beast tamed | A handler of level 6 or more with a love of animals, where the land has great beasts (huge ones, or as wild as a thrumbo) | One of them is theirs, bonded or as its master

A herd worth the name | Someone who loves animals, the herdmaster, or a keen grower when there's a herd already | The colony's livestock reaches 8 head, or 4 more than when they set out, whichever is more
An animal that knows everything | A handler with a love of animals, with an animal of their own or one going spare | An animal of theirs has learned everything it can be taught
Story | How it starts | How it ends

An old companion | A bonded animal grows old (four fifths of its kind's life) | Quiet hours together, slow afternoons, one more good day. Its death ends the story, without the usual "came to nothing": a farewell instead.

Raised by hand | A young animal of the colony's loses its mother, and a handler who loves animals, a kind soul, a child or the herdmaster takes it on | Hours at its side and handling practice; once it's grown, the two may bond

The stray | A calm wild animal hangs about the colony and someone leaves scraps out | If it stays a few days, it's marked for taming and the story ends when it's the colony's. If it leaves the land, it's over.

A feud with an animal | Someone else's named animal and a colonist take against each other, often after it stole their food | Open war (a small bad mood), then an uneasy truce, then a friendship neither will admit to

li.heading: Dilemmas

table.li: Dilemma | When | The choices

The herd or the stores | Food for fewer than 6 days, with a herd of 4 or more eating from the same stores | Cull about a quarter of the herd (1 to 4 head, never the last 2), tighten everyone's belts, turn the weakest out to forage, or let the handler choose. A cull is real: the handlers slaughter the marked animals.
A raider in the crops | Spring to autumn, a wild grazer in or near the fields | Send the hunters, watch the fields at night, try to tame it, or let it eat. The crops it eats are lost.

Medicine for an animal | One of the colony's animals is ill, with 1 to 15 medicine in store | The good medicine, herbs only, its person nursing it through, or nothing. The answer sets its medical care.

Something at the pens | A predator on the land near a herd of 2 or more | Hunt it, keep watch at the pens, bring the herd in close, or leave it be. A predator left alone may break in and take one of the herd.

A bond against the ideoligion | With Ideology: a colonist bonded to an animal, and another whose ideoligion abhors such bonds | Stand by the bond, keep the animal out of the faithful one's way, give it to someone else, or ask for a blessing

li.after: Nobody's own animal, and nothing bonded or named, is ever culled, turned out or lost.

li.heading: The herd's year
li.text:
Three customs can become traditions, like the council's seasonal ones: the lambing watch in spring, when an animal of the herd is in lamb (the whole colony takes turns at the pens through the night), and shearing day in spring or summer, when there are animals to shear or milk (the whole colony at the pens and something to eat in the sun after); both ask for a herd of 2 or more. And bringing the herd home: before the winter (the cold coming in the fall), in a cold snap, or the day after a raid, with a herd of 3 or more, a barn or a pen for it, and 2 or more of it out in the open. It's asked in that moment, after the usual gap between questions. Held, a work party of up to 5 goes out with ropes: each puts a rope on an animal grazing in the open, the game's own way, and walks it into its pen or the barn (handling practice and contentment, no mood). One person can do it alone instead, or the herd can be left to find its own way in, which worries the one who asked. The answer "bring the herd in close" when a predator stalks the pens sends two out the same way.
On the calendar, the colony's first foal is written down the day it's born and kept as a feast, and a beloved animal's day, for a bonded animal that died after a year or more with the colony or fighting for its person, is kept as a remembrance by those who loved it (up to 3).

li.heading: Dreams and setbacks
li.text:
People dream of the herd, of animals that talk, of something at the pens, of riding (children), of a beloved animal grown old, and, after a bonded animal dies, of it coming back.
Two setbacks come from the pens: "one of the herd was taken" (-3 for 4 days) and "the pen was broken into" (-2 for 3 days), when a predator the council left alone, or let close, gets in.

li.heading: The herd's leader and its line
li.text: Once the colony's herd is four head or more, it has a leader: the eldest adult of the kind there is most of, named (if it had no name) by its keeper, the herdmaster, or whoever is best with animals, who speaks to it at the pens. A letter tells it, and the chronicle keeps it. From then on the leader's line is counted: a calf born to the leader is the second generation, its calf the third, and the first calf of each new generation is news. When the leader grows old (four fifths of its kind's years) its last season is told, and the keeper sits with it at the pens of an evening. When it dies, the herd has lost its leader: the keeper takes it hard for a few days, and within a day or two the herd follows a new one, the old leader's own blood first if any is grown, else the eldest of the many, and a new line begins.

li.heading: The first calf of spring
li.text: The first animal born to the herd each spring is a moment: a letter, a small glad thought for everyone, and the keeper walks down to the pens and stays a while until it stands. (The colony's very first foal is still written down on the calendar, as before.)

li.heading: At a glance
li.text: The Overview page's card "The herd and the land" shows who leads the herd, of which line and generation, whether the old leader is in its last season, the beast the colony watches and what it has made of it, a shiny rumour on the wind, and the neighbours settled for good. In development mode, "Rimfolk: check myself" says what stands between the herd and a leader or between a wild animal and a name right now.

li.heading: A beast that stays
li.text: A wild animal of some size that stays on the colony's land three days running, a wolf, a bear, a stag, a boar, not an insect and not a great beast (those have their own stories), is given a name: a child names it, when there is one, else someone with a love of animals, else anyone, and a letter tells the colony. From then on whoever sees it says so, in their own words. Four days after the naming the council is asked what to make of it, and again every eight days while it stays, three times at most. Leave food out for it, and the one who named it carries meat (for a meat-eater) or hay or raw food out to where it is and leaves it; keep everyone close, and the best shot keeps a watch at the gate that night; send the hunters, and the hunters go out after it; let the namer try to tame it, and it goes on the handlers' list; let it be; or drive it off, and two go out at dusk with torches while it makes for the edge of the land. Fed outweighs feared in what the colonists say of it. After fifteen days it is part of the land and the story closes, the namer glad of it; hunted, tamed, driven off, dead or moved on, it closes sooner, and the chronicle keeps how. Another beast can take its place twenty days later; one whose story has closed is never taken up again.
